messages.subject: [amelia] Technical Support for Amelia II
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sirs,

   We are a group of researchers at the University of HK. We have  
newly installed the R and Amelia II in the PC.

   Once I started the Amelia it always prompted me saying that I did
   not specify the R route in Amelia.ini file.

   I have then opened the file and put down the below route , yet it
   still  doesn't work. Any suggestions?

   RPath="C:\Program Files\R\R-2.7.1\bin\Rcmd.exe"

   Thanks.

   Regards,

   KK Mak
-

messages.subject: [amelia] Technical Support for Amelia II
messages.body_plain:
Hi KK Mak,

The amelia.ini file should read:

RPath=C:\Program Files\R\R-2.7.1

That is, it only needs to point to the directory that contains the R
version you are using, not the actual R exe. We'll update the
documentation to make this more clear. Sorry about that.

Thanks for the catch,
matt.

messages.subject: [amelia] start problem in vista32
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

 

I have problems getting amelia started. I installed as described. After
clicking the Amelia.bat the following error occurred: "system cannot find.
c:\program files\ameliaview\lib\invisible.vbs" 

 

I checked that the file is in the folder. This is on a pc on which vista 32
is installed.

 

To check I installed the Amelia software also on a PC which is running
windows 2000. this time no problem. 

 

I would be thankful if somebody could advice me how to run the program on
the pc with vista. 

 

Thanks

 

Alexander

messages.subject: [amelia] start problem in vista32
messages.body_plain:
Hello Alexander,

There hasn't been any development of Amelia in Vista quite yet. As you
have found, the Windows launcher is probably the most likely place to
break. While I haven't had a copy of Vista to play around with, I
imagine the following might work better. Open up R and type:

library(Amelia)
AmeliaView()

That will bring up the same GUI that the launcher opens. Like I said,
I'm not totally confident this will work, but I think it should.

hope that helps,
matt.
